# Native storage-error contract build

Source: Turso v0.8.2, commit `5c168be5ef6a32ac966daf5983502a4f694b37ad`.
Applied patch SHA-256:
`eadb14ec88ac351c938908443bcb89da324411e4eb8f8d068b3cc755fc0808ae`.
Cargo.lock SHA-256:
`cca554b407bc4d3ae21bab93f44b7fa2e7091ab89daddb66ba021b390dd59f6b`.

Both builds used Rust 1.88.0, locked dependencies, package
`turso_sync_sdk_kit` and profile `release-official`. Packaging removed the
compiler's runtime search paths with patchelf 0.15.2. Original compiler output
and full build/ELF receipts are retained separately from the release copies.

| Runtime | Packaged library SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| linux-x64 | `a8e66163067435de33627e2231f1f409a78fb5e2ed1a10ade478a815d4ad702f` |
| linux-arm64 | `c14fe3965580b762fd4f8d128a8b5043c393ad3e0ab98559875175917b8dccb4` |

Both packaged libraries retain the marker and all 29 required sync exports,
have no RPATH/RUNPATH or absolute DT_NEEDED entries, and require at most
GLIBC 2.35. The marker returned 1 with production runtime GLIBC 2.43: x64 in
the chiseled runtime container and ARM through user-mode qemu 10.2.4 against
the ARM production runtime libraries. No serving host or binfmt registration
was changed. This establishes native loading and the marker contract, not
database tamper handling or managed single-file loading.
